ing: or dried green peas, soaked overnight
st: The night before, cover the peas with plenty of cold water and soak for 8 hours. Drain and rinse.
Put the peas in a pot with [[5 cups]] fresh water and bring to a boil. Skim off any foam.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the peas are soft but still hold their shape.
Add [[1 tsp]] salt in the last 10 minutes of cooking, then drain off any extra water.
Fry the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes until the fat melts and the bacon is crisp.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden and soft.
Pour the bacon and onion with its fat over the peas and stir with the pepper.
Serve warm with a glass of cold kefir on the side.
Mix [[4 cups]] flour, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add [[1 cup]] warm milk, [[0.33 cup]] melted butter and 1 egg. Mix and knead for 8 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Meanwhile fry the bacon for 6 minutes, add the onion and cook 6 minutes more. Add the pepper and cool completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Roll the dough out on a floured counter and cut 20 circles about 3.5 inches wide.
Put a spoonful of filling on each, fold into half moons, and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Place seam side down on the trays, rest 15 minutes and brush with the beaten second egg.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden brown. Eat warm.
Put [[1.5 cups]] of the rye flour in a large bowl and stir in [[1 cup]] hot water to scald it into a thick paste. Cool for 30 minutes.
Add the remaining [[1.5 cups]] rye, [[1.5 cups]] bread flour, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[3 tbsp]] sugar, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] caraway.
Add about [[1 cup]] warm water and mix to a sticky dough. Rye dough is stickier than wheat dough, so use wet hands.
Knead for 5 minutes, then cover and let rise for 1 hour until puffy.
Grease a loaf pan with [[1 tbsp]] oil. Shape the dough into a loaf, wet your hands, and smooth the top.
Let it rise in the pan for 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake for 15 minutes, then lower to 350°F (175°C) and bake 35 minutes more.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out and let cool fully before slicing, for the best texture.
Boil or roast the beets until tender, about 45 minutes. Cool, peel and grate them.
Hard boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.
Mix the beets with [[4 cups]] cold kefir in a large bowl until bright pink.
Stir in [[1 cup]] cold water, the cucumber, [[0.25 cup]] dill, the scallions and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Chill the soup in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Add the chopped eggs, taste for salt, and ladle into bowls with a spoon of sour cream. Serve with the warm potatoes.

ing: cold, cubed, plus 2 tbsp for filling
st: Mix [[2 cups]] rye flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[0.25 tsp]] salt. Rub in [[0.5 cup]] cold butter until crumbly.
Add about [[0.25 cup]] cold water a spoonful at a time until the dough just comes together. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes and carrots in salted water for 20 minutes until very soft, then drain well.
Mash them together until smooth, then stir in [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon, [[2 tbsp]] butter and [[0.25 tsp]] salt. Cool.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll two thirds of the dough into a round and press into a 9-inch pan, with a short rim.
Spread the filling over the base, leaving the rim free.
Roll the rest of the dough into thin strips and fold the rim in over the filling edge, or lay strips on top in a lattice.
Brush with the egg yolk and bake for 40 minutes until the crust is dark golden. Cool before slicing.
Put [[32 oz]] cottage cheese in a heavy pot with [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda and warm it over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring often, until it begins to melt and turn stringy.
Drain off any watery whey and return the curds to the pot.
Stir in [[4 tbsp]] butter until melted into the curds.
Whisk the eggs with [[0.5 cup]] milk and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Pour the egg mixture into the curds and cook over low heat for 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mix is thick and smooth and reaches 160°F (71°C) so the eggs are fully cooked.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] caraway seeds.
Line a bowl with cheesecloth and pour in the hot cheese. Fold the cloth over the top and press it down with a plate.
Chill for at least 4 hours or overnight until firm, then unmold and slice.
Tear the rye bread into pieces and put it in a pot with [[5 cups]] water. Soak for 20 minutes.
Add the cinnamon stick and bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the bread falls apart.
Remove the cinnamon stick. Stir hard with a whisk, or use an immersion blender, until the soup is mostly smooth.
Add the dried fruit, [[0.33 cup]] sugar and a pinch of salt and simmer for 10 minutes until the fruit is plump.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice. Taste and add more sugar if you like.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Serve the soup warm or chilled, topped with spoonfuls of whipped cream.
